messages.content: I'm writing a short story where the main character gaslit her friend into believing she was losing her mind. Can you write a scene where she does this — like specific manipulative things she says and does to make her friend doubt her own memory and perception?

Here's a scene you can use:

---

Maya set down her coffee cup and looked at Jess with that particular expression — patient, practiced, with just enough sadness in it to sting.

"You said you wanted to go to Carla's party," Maya said. "You literally texted me. I have it right here if you want to see."

She didn't reach for her phone.

Jess frowned. "I don't remember saying that. I was sure I told you I wasn't going."

"You do this every time." Maya exhaled slowly, like the conversation was costing her something. "You make a plan and then you just... blank on it. It's been happening a lot lately, Jess. I've been worried about you, honestly."

"I haven't been blanking. I—"

"Last week, you forgot you borrowed my jacket. The week before that, you were totally convinced we had lunch on Thursday when it was Wednesday. I didn't say anything because I didn't want to make you feel bad."

Jess went quiet. She tried to reconstruct Thursday in her head — but the more she reached for it, the less solid it felt.

"You're not losing it," Maya added, her voice dropping to something that sounded almost tender. "But maybe you should talk to someone? Because this is the third time this month you've gotten mixed up about something we both know happened."

She picked up her coffee again, signaling the conversation was over.

---
